summary: Steve Odin is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Stony Brook University under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey (~1975–1980), later holding a postdoctoral fellowship there (~1980–1982) and becoming Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 1982.

Steven Collins (1950–2018) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich, taught at the University of Bristol (~1980–1987), and was named Chester D. Tripp Professor in the Humanities at the University of Chicago in 1991.

Steven Edward Lindquist is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under Patrick Olivelle in 2005, also studying under traditional teachers, and later held a post at Concordia University.

Steven Heine works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Temple University, as well as under Shudo Ishii. His posts include Villanova University, La Salle University, Pennsylvania State University (~1991–1997), and Florida International University (Professor, 1997).

Steven Lukes (born 1941) is a philosopher and sociologist. He studied at the University of Oxford under Edward Evan Evans-Pritchard, served as Fellow and Tutor at Balliol College (1966–1987), and held professorships at Florence, Siena, LSE, and New York University (~2001–2021).

Steven Neal Weinberger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA at Amherst College and his MA and PhD (2003) at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, also studying under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers, and held a post at Virginia.
Stewart McFarlane is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology who held posts at Lancaster University, attested in 1991 and in the Department of Religious Studies in 2001.

Sthaneshwar Timalsina is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, San Diego State University (~2005–2018), and Stony Brook University (~2018).

Stig Wikander (1908–1983) was a Swedish scholar of Indology, Iranian-Central Asian, and religious studies. He completed an MA at Uppsala University under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, served as docent at Lund University (1941–1953), and held the Sanskrit chair at Uppsala (1953–1974).

Stuart H. Blackburn is an Indologist who completed his education at Wesleyan University (~1962–1966) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1975–1980). He held a post at SOAS University of London from around 1993 to 2011.

Stuart Piggott (1910–1996) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned a graduate diploma at University College London and the UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1934–1936), subsequently holding a long-term academic appointment at the University of Edinburgh (~1946–1977).

Stuart Ray Sarbacker is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy degree in 2001 at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he studied under doctoral supervisor David M. Knipe.

Su Bai (1922–2018) was a specialist in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He pursued graduate studies at Peking University (1940–1944) under scholars including Rong Geng and Yongtong Tang, and subsequently served as a professor at Peking University from 1948 to 2004.

Subhadradis Diskul (1923–2003) was a Thai archaeologist and historian. After studies at Chulalongkorn, École du Louvre, and the University of London, he served as a curator at Bangkok's National Museum, professor of archaeology, and rector (1976–1986) at Silpakorn University.

Subhash Kak is an Indologist and engineering scholar. After completing his Ph.D. under Pavaguda V. Indiresan at IIT Delhi (~1967–1970), he held professorships at Louisiana State University (1979) and later became Regents Professor at Oklahoma State University (2007).

Subrata K. Mitra (born 1949) studied at Utkal University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Rochester. He held posts at the universities of Hull, Nottingham, California, Berkeley, Heidelberg (~1994–2014), and the National University of Singapore (2015–2018).

Sucheng Chan (born 1941) is a historian who completed studies at Swarthmore College (~1959–1963), the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1963–1965), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1969–1973). She served as a professor at UC Santa Barbara (~1984–2002).
Sudan Shakya is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held a post as a professor at Shuchiin University, attested between 2013 and 2017 as well as in 2026.

Sudhir Kakar (1938–2024) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Gujarat University, Mannheim, Vienna, and the Sigmund-Freud-Institut. His posts included Harvard, IIM Ahmedabad, and IIT Delhi (1976–1977), alongside numerous visiting appointments, including at INSEAD (1994–2013).

Sudhākara Dvivedī (1855–1910) was an Indologist who studied under Devakṛṣṇa. He served as librarian (1883) and later professor of mathematics and astrology (1890) and department head (1898–1905) at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, also working at Sanskrit College and University.
